minutes.headline: Sewer budget for town meeting draws on retained earnings; no rate hike now, but one is expected next year
minutes.summary: The Sewer Commission reviewed the Comprehensive Wastewater Management Plan, discussed recruiting new commission members, and heard that the FY25 fourth-quarter billing run was completed successfully despite Munis software problems. The bulk of the meeting covered warrant articles for the upcoming town meeting, including a sewer budget balanced with retained earnings and no rate increase this year, plus fund transfers for OPEB, I&I, and reserve capacity; the commission also learned a candidate has been recommended for hire as assistant to the business manager.

what_happened.line: The FY26 sewer budget going to town meeting is balanced with retained earnings and carries no rate increase this year.
The director told the commission that rising costs mean sewer rates will likely need to increase next year.
Warrant articles moving money into the OPEB, inflow-and-infiltration, and reserve capacity funds are slated for the town meeting consent calendar as non-controversial.
A Munis billing error was caught and corrected during fourth-quarter reconciliation, and a resident's concern about uncollected sewer billing was raised again.
The commission recommended a candidate for hire as assistant to the business manager, with a start date expected in late May.

why_it_matters: No sewer rate hike is proposed this year, but the director's warning means residents should expect one to come up for a vote next budget cycle.
The sewer budget and three fund-transfer articles go before town meeting, where they are expected to pass without debate on the consent calendar.
Recurring software errors and unresolved uncollected billing touch the accuracy of individual sewer bills, separate from the budget vote itself.
